name: Charles W. Sleeper
role: Vice president of the N. P. Refrigerator Car Co.
bio: Charles W. Sleeper was elected vice president of the N. P. Refrigerator Car Co. at a directors' meeting in St. Paul on February 5, 1884. Through 1884 he traveled constantly on company business to St. Paul, Duluth and Helena, and the paper called him "the irrepressible and indefatigable vice-president" when he left for Duluth on the Marquis' special train in August. In April 1884 he moved at a round-up meeting that a delegate be named from each range. In November 1884 he went to the Black Hills on business for the stage line and came back impressed with the progress there. He left Medora at the end of 1884, and by February 1885 he was at his home in Binghamton, N. Y.
